6 Media security

6.1 The officer in charge of each police station at which interviews with suspects are
recorded shall make arrangements for master recordings to be kept securely and
their movements accounted for on the same basis as material which may be used for
evidential purposes, in accordance with force standing orders. See Note 6A

6.2 A police officer has no authority to break the seal on a master recording required for
criminal trial or appeal proceedings. If it is necessary to gain access to the master
recording, the police officer shall arrange for its seal to be broken in the presence
of a representative of the Crown Prosecution Service. The defendant or their legal
adviser should be informed and given a reasonable opportunity to be present. If the
defendant or their legal representative is present they shall be invited to reseal and
sign the master recording. If either refuses or neither is present this should be done
by the representative of the Crown Prosecution Service. See Notes 6B and 6C
